_note: Dissertations index on the Lounge sample page (lounge/sample/). TITLES AND ONE-SENTENCE DESCRIPTIONS ONLY: the full texts are members-only on Patreon and never go in this repo. Fields: title, description (one sentence, shown verbatim), tier (label, e.g. 'Lounge Member and up'), patreon_url (https://www.patreon.com/... post link, or null), status ('live' or 'coming'). An entry shows 'Read on Patreon (members only)' only when status is 'live' AND patreon_url is set; otherwise 'Coming soon to the Lounge'. releases: list of release-page slugs (release/<slug>/) the piece is the dissertation for; when status is 'live' AND patreon_url is set, each of those pages shows a 'Read the dissertation (members only)' link to the post. Use [] for companion pieces that should only appear in the index. Order = display order. Rebuild with python3 tools/build_pages.py.

dissertations.title: A Dissertation on the Historical References in the Lyrics of “Freeborn” by bfo.mantis
dissertations.description: This piece reconstructs the five refusals the single names (Lilburne 1638, Luther at Worms 1521, Douglass 1833–34, Parks 1955, and Havel 1977–89) and shows how the song turns them into proof that freeborn status comes with the first breath.

dissertations.title: An Analysis of One Freeborn Man
dissertations.description: This short companion essay reads the single “Freeborn” and the album One Man INVICTUS together as one continuous demonstration that the freeborn act is the refusal to kneel.

dissertations.title: A Dissertation on the Lyrics and History of One Man INVICTUS by bfo.mantis
dissertations.description: This album-level study follows the stands of the fifteen tracks, from the Tank Man, Thich Quang Duc, and Desmond Doss to Joan of Arc, Leonidas, and the closing prayer, and measures how the lyrics compress each one into the album's “One Man” argument.

dissertations.title: A Dissertation on the History and Lyrics of “Cake on the Plate” by bfo.mantis
dissertations.description: This piece traces the song's Sparta from Thermopylae through Pausanias, Lysander's gold and Leuctra to its collapse in numbers, and shows how the lyric moves the city's fall from the gates to the table and hands that choice to the listener.

dissertations.title: A Dissertation on the History and Lyrics of “For Your Own Good” by bfo.mantis
dissertations.description: This piece reconstructs the cases the single names, from Juvenal’s bread and games and the English hearth tax to Prohibition and the wartime camps, and traces the long argument against power used “for your own good” to show how the song strips the velvet from the blade and hands the listener a single spoken No.
